text:
sara: Quick sync after the RFC review. Two unresolved pieces: how do we represent actor provenance when a request passes through proxies, and whatxact telemetry fields are required for efficient post-incident analysis?

ned: For provenance I propose an `actor_chain` array in the audit store (not top-level telemetry). In telemetry we should emit a compact `actor_prov` token (hash of chain) + `chain_depth` int. Full chain kept only in TTLed audit logs.

priya: Agree on minimal telemetry. Also want explicit `api_key_scope` in events: one of `org`, `project`, `org:project`, `global`. That avoids parsing freeform scopes later.

jamie: Also add `decision_id` (uuid) for correlating logs/traces. Helps when a single request spawns multiple policy checks.

karen: Ops point: we need deny-flood detection. Telemetry should include `deny_reason_code` (enum) and `is_rate_limited` boolean so the rules engine can signal emergency sampling.

ash: (ops-bot): current pipeline uses topic `audits.auth.v1`. If we add `auth_decision` tag we can route denies to the high-retention topic. Will need schema bump.

ash: also suggest a sampling policy: 100% for denies, 100% for admin/token exchange endpoints, adaptive sampling for suspicious IPs (10x sample), base sample 2% for allows.

priya: retention: telemetry (hashed IDs) 90 days, raw audit store (unhashed chains/ids) 14 days default, legal can request extension per-case. We'll loop them in.

sara: Draft telemetry payload (compact, proto-friendly):
```
auth_decision_v2 {
  decision_id: "uuid"
  outcome: "allow"|"deny"
  decision_ts: 1710000000
  decision_latency_ms: 8
  policy_hash: "sha1"
  matched_conditions: ["ip_reputation","role_mismatch"]
  decision_source: "local"|"remote"
  actor_kind: "user"|"service"|"operator"
  actor_hash: "sha256"
  actor_prov_token: "sha256"
  chain_depth: 2
  api_key_scope: "project"
  org_id: "org-123"
  project_id: "proj-456"
  endpoint: "/v1/embeddings"
  cache_hit: true
  deny_reason_code: "ROLE_MISMATCH"
  sample_rate: 0.02
  storage_tier: "hot"
}
```

jamie: small nit: use `policy_id` (stable) + `policy_hash` (for quick diff) so we can surface which policy changed.

ned: on actor_hash: use salted hashes per-tenant to prevent cross-org correlation. Salt rotation policy needs ops input.

ash: for salted hash we'd need the salt available in the agents that emit telemetry. ops prefers deterministic per-cluster salt and rotation via KMS. Keeps verification internal only.

priya: regarding middleware and propagation: propose `propagate` boolean and `propagate_mode` enum (`full`|`minimal`|`none`). `full` emits actor_chain into internal logs, `minimal` emits only actor_hash+prov_token to telemetry.

sara: example middleware YAML: 
```
auth_middleware:
  propagate: true
  propagate_mode: minimal
  emit_fields: [decision_id,outcome,actor_kind,actor_hash,actor_prov_token,org_id,project_id,endpoint,policy_id,policy_hash]
  deny_handling: {log_full: true, alert: true}
  sampling: {allows: 0.02, denies: 1.0, admin: 1.0}
```

karen: one more: make `policy_cache_hit` mandatory; we use that to triage slowness.

jamie: agree. Also include `auth_flow` string to indicate phase (ingress, post-auth, token-exchange) for better aggregation.

priya: privacy check: hashed actor identifiers and prov tokens okay for external telemetry. Any unanonymized material goes to internal audit only. I'll track legal review.

ned: implementation note: add a `decision_context` header to internal traces containing decision_id + sampled=true, so traces can pull matching telemetry.

ash: ops: will prepare a schema migration plan and topic changes. ETA Monday. We will need to backfill short-term dashboards.

sara: plan: ned drafts follow-up doc with final schema + sampling matrix; priy a clears privacy; ops does infra plan. Lock decisions next Weds. Thanks all.
